title: Why do traffic lights have three colours?
examples: Why do we have to stop at the red light?
What does the yellow light mean for cars?
Can we go through the lights if they are flashing?

explain.say: Look at the red light first. Red means you must stop your vehicle right away.

draw.text: Why do traffic lights have three colours?

explain.say: Next, the amber light comes on. Amber means you should get ready to stop.
Then, the green light shines bright. Green means it is safe for you to go through.
If the light is red, you stop. If it turns green, you can go. Amber means be careful.
When you cross the road, you must watch the lights. If it is green, you can walk across safely.
A common mistake is thinking you can go when the light is flashing. Always wait for a clear green light.

faq.q: Why does the light change colours?
faq.a: The light changes colours to tell everyone what to do. It keeps traffic moving safely for all people.
asks: What is the purpose of the colours?

faq.q: What should I do if the light is flashing red?
faq.a: If the light is flashing red, it means you must stop and wait. You should wait until it turns green.
asks: What does a flashing red light mean?

faq.q: Does amber mean I can go a little bit?
faq.a: No, amber means you should prepare to stop. You should slow down and get ready to stop your vehicle.
asks: Is amber a warning to go?
What is the rule for amber light?

faq.q: Can I cross if the light is just yellow?
faq.a: You should only cross when the light is clearly green for pedestrians. Amber is for cars to prepare to stop.
asks: Is yellow light okay for crossing?
When is it safe to cross the road?

faq.q: Do the lights work the same in all countries?
faq.a: Most places use red for stop and green for go. However, some places might use different colours for signals.
asks: Are traffic lights the same everywhere?
Do all countries use these three colours?

facts: Red light always means stop for vehicles.
Green light means it is safe to proceed.
Amber light warns that the light is about to change.
Traffic lights help keep roads safe for everyone.

quiz.say: If the light is red, you must:
quiz.why: Red is the universal sign for stopping all movement.

wrong.0: This is tempting because slowing down seems safe, but red means a full stop.
wrong.1: This is wrong because waiting is not enough; you must physically stop.
wrong.2: This is dangerous because it ignores the clear stop signal.

quiz.say: When the light turns amber, you should:
quiz.why: Amber is a warning to slow down and get ready for red.

wrong.0: This ignores the warning that the signal is changing soon.
wrong.1: Ignoring signals is never safe or correct.
wrong.3: Speeding up is the opposite of what the warning means.

quiz.say: If you see green for walking, it means:

options.show: You must wait for another light
options.say: You must wait for another light

quiz.why: Green for pedestrians means the road is clear for you to walk.

wrong.0: Green for walkers means the cars must stop for you.
wrong.1: If it is green for you, you should cross now.
wrong.2: While you should be careful, green means it is safe to cross properly.
